title: The category of Harish–Chandra modules
notes: The notes describe a compatible action of \(G\) and \(\mathfrak g\), with finite multiplicities on restriction to \(K\), and denote the category by \(\mathcal C\).
statement: For a real linear connected semisimple group \(G\), maximal compact subgroup \(K\), and complexified Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), a Harish--Chandra module is a finitely generated \(U(\mathfrak g)\)-module with compatible locally finite algebraic \(K\)-action and finite multiplicity of every irreducible \(K\)-type.
reconstruction: The notes here do not require a global action of \(G\) on the algebraic module; compatibility is between \(\mathfrak g\) and \(K\). Finite generation is imported from the next lecture, explicitly marked.
fate: \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} state the full definition. The manuscript supplies finite generation on P000721; it is needed in the theorem that follows.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Algebraization of a bounded part of the Harish–Chandra category
notes: Gelfand asks for a description of \(\mathcal C\) by representations of an associative algebra with finitely many generators and relations.
statement: For a bounded connected open subset \(D\) of the spectrum \(\Theta\) of the center \(Z(U(\mathfrak g))\), seek an algebra \(Q\), finite as a module over the center, for which the category of Harish--Chandra modules with generalized infinitesimal characters in \(D\) is equivalent to the corresponding support-restricted finite-dimensional \(Q\)-module category.
reconstruction: The bounded central-support restriction is supplied by the theorem actually proved; the opening formulation does not state it.
fate: The precise affirmative theorem is \citet[\S3, Theorem~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1}, presented to the Paris Academy on 9 January 1978 and printed in March 1978. It is local in central support, not an equivalence between the entire category and all modules over one finite-dimensional algebra.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The Lorentz-group matrix-pair precedent
notes: The notes recall the Gelfand--Ponomarev reduction for the Lorentz group to two operators \(A,B\) satisfying \(AB=BA=0\).
statement: The cited precedent concerns explicit finite-dimensional matrix problems describing suitable Harish--Chandra blocks for the Lorentz group. The relations \(AB=BA=0\) alone, without the block, support, nilpotence and equivalence conventions, do not specify the whole representation category.
fate: The later account \citet[\S6, case \(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb C)\)]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} confirms an explicit local matrix-order model. This verifies the direction of the precedent but not an unrestricted equivalence with the bare two-operator category.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Central characters and support
notes: The center \(Z\) has spectrum \(\Theta\); the notes attach a subset \(\operatorname{supp}V\subset\Theta\) to a module.
statement: For a Harish--Chandra module \(V\), its central support is the finite set of characters \(\theta:Z\to\mathbb C\) for which the generalized \(\theta\)-eigenspace is nonzero. Finite generation and admissibility imply that \(V\) is annihilated by a finite-codimensional ideal of \(Z\).
fate: \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} formulate this central-finiteness statement and use it to define the categories attached to subsets of \(\Theta\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Decomposition by generalized infinitesimal character
notes: The category attached to a set of characters is written as a sum of the single-character categories; distinct characters do not interact.
statement: Every Harish--Chandra module is a finite direct sum of its generalized central-character submodules. A homomorphism between modules with disjoint generalized central supports is zero. The category is therefore the finite-support direct sum of its generalized-character blocks.
fate: This is the central decomposition used in \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1}. It follows from the primary decomposition of a module over a finite-dimensional quotient of the commutative center.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: An algebra finite over the center
notes: For bounded \(D\), the notes state an equivalence \(\mathcal C_D\simeq\operatorname{mod}Q\), where \(Q\) is finite over \(Z\).
statement: For bounded connected open \(D\subset\Theta\), there exists a \(Z\)-algebra \(Q\), finite over \(Z\), and a \(Z\)-linear equivalence \(\mathcal C_D\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_D Q\), where the right side consists of finite-dimensional modules whose central support lies in \(D\).
fate: Exactly \citet[\S3, Theorem~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1}. The later analytic localization \(Q\otimes_Z\mathcal O(D)\) permits a category of all finite-dimensional modules of that localized algebra; this is a different formulation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: A rank-three analytic matrix order for PSL2(R)
notes: The example uses \(3\times3\) matrix-valued analytic functions with specified entries vanishing at a distinguished point.
statement: Near the regular infinitesimal character of the trivial representation of \(\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb R)\), the block category is represented by a matrix order \(R\subset M_3(\mathcal O(D))\). In the published left-module convention, with rows and columns labeled \(-1,0,1\), the entries \(a_{-1,0},a_{1,0},a_{-1,1},a_{1,-1}\) vanish at the centered parameter \(z=0\).
reconstruction: The published parameter and left-module convention are stated explicitly; the notebook changes orientation in later diagrams.
fate: \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} give the exact three-type order in March 1978. The notebook\textquotesingle s row/column placement must be compared up to permutation and opposite-algebra convention, not silently identified entry by entry.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Finite generation and admissibility
notes: The definition now requires finite generation over \(U(\mathfrak g)\), finite-dimensional \(K\)-isotypic multiplicity spaces and compatible actions; Harish-Chandra\textquotesingle s theorem is invoked.
statement: A Harish--Chandra module has the three conditions just stated. For irreducible admissible representations in the usual reductive representation-theoretic setting, the \(K\)-finite vectors form such a module. This is not a theorem about arbitrary representations without a topology or admissibility hypothesis.
fate: \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} use this precise algebraic category. The classical admissibility theorem is background to the construction, rather than the novel local-algebra statement.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The support criterion is a character, not its value
notes: The support condition is written with \(\theta(z)\), followed by a common central eigenvector condition.
statement: A character \(\theta\in\Theta\) lies in the support of \(V\) if its generalized eigenspace is nonzero. Since the central action factors through a finite-dimensional commutative algebra, this is equivalent to the existence of a nonzero vector on which every \(z\in Z\) acts as \(\theta(z)\). The scalar \(\theta(z)\) itself is not a point of \(\Theta\).
fate: The correctly typed support definition appears in \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Separation of disjoint central supports
notes: The notes repeat that modules with separated support have no morphisms between them and split into single-support pieces.
statement: If \(\operatorname{supp}V\cap\operatorname{supp}W=\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname{Hom}_{(\mathfrak g,K)}(V,W)=0\); the primary decomposition of the central action is canonical and finite for each object.
fate: The same construction is used in \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} and recurs here as preparation for a local equivalence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Equivalence of categories
notes: The notes explicitly say \ru{не совпад., а изоморфно!}: the composites are isomorphic to the identity, and the diagrams commute.
statement: An equivalence consists of functors \(F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D\), \(G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C\), and natural isomorphisms \(GF\cong\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal C}\), \(FG\cong\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal D}\). Equality on the nose is unnecessary.
fate: This is exactly the standard categorical meaning of equivalence used in \citet[\S3]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1}; the recovered complete scan of P000722 confirms the distinction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Morita equivalence for a full matrix algebra
notes: Finite-dimensional vector spaces are identified with modules over \(M_2(\mathbb C)\), by tensoring with the defining representation and recovering a multiplicity space.
statement: The functors \(E\mapsto\mathbb C^2\otimes E\) and \(V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{M_2(\mathbb C)}(\mathbb C^2,V)\) are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between finite-dimensional vector spaces and finite-dimensional left \(M_2(\mathbb C)\)-modules.
fate: The notebook gives an elementary Morita example; the general equivalence setting is that of \citet[\S3]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1}. The recovered complete P000722 scan confirms the two categories.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Nice analytic algebras
notes: A \ru{приятная} algebra lies inside matrix-valued analytic functions and has the full matrix algebra as generic fiber.
statement: Let \(E\) be a connected complex manifold and \(B\) a finite-dimensional semisimple algebra. A nice algebra is an \(\mathcal O(E)\)-subalgebra \(R\subset B\otimes\mathcal O(E)\), containing scalar functions and becoming \(B\otimes\mathcal M(E)\) after extension to the field of meromorphic functions; the published definition includes the required finiteness over \(\mathcal O(E)\).
fate: \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} give the definition and distinguish the stronger freeness condition called strongly nice.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The local nice-algebra theorem
notes: The category is described by a nice algebra on a domain with dimension equal to the real split rank.
statement: If \(\theta\) is a regular infinitesimal character, a sufficiently small neighborhood \(D\) of \(\theta\) has \(\mathcal C_D\) equivalent to the finite-dimensional modules of a nice analytic algebra. The parameter manifold has dimension equal to the real split rank; in the split case the formulation uses \(E=D\).
reconstruction: Regularity and the sufficiently small neighborhood are essential hypotheses supplied from the published theorem, not visible in the notebook formulation.
fate: \citet[\S2, Theorem~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} prove this with the regular-character and local-neighborhood hypotheses. The theorem is not stated there for arbitrary singular characters or arbitrary bounded domains.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The sl2 Casimir has a sign inconsistency
notes: The quadratic central element is written with a negative \(H^2\) term.
statement: For \([H,E_+]=2E_+\), \([H,E_-]=-2E_-\), \([E_+,E_-]=H\), the element \(C=4E_-E_++H^2+2H\) is central. Replacing \(+H^2\) by \(-H^2\) does not yield a central element in these conventions.
reconstruction: The correction uses the positive standard matrix generators on the recovered complete P000722 scan and the differential realization on P000728. The recovered scan independently confirms the minus sign before \(H^2\).
fate: The Casimir and rank-one principal-series facts here are classical background, not first results of the 1978 local-category papers. The local parameter in \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} is a shifted normalized central character. The explicit sign diagnosis follows directly from the Lie brackets and is an editorial calculation, not a claim that the published paper printed the notebook formula.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Generators of the rank-one matrix order
notes: Nine generators are given as matrix units, with selected off-diagonal units multiplied by the local coordinate \(z\).
statement: If \(R\subset M_3(\mathcal O(D))\) is the indicated order, its \(\mathcal O(D)\)-module generators are diagonal matrix units, ordinary matrix units in unrestricted positions, and \(z e_{ij}\) in positions required to vanish at \(z=0\). Multiplication is inherited from \(e_{ij}e_{kl}=\delta_{jk}e_{il}\).
fate: This is the explicit order of \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2}, up to the notebook\textquotesingle s changing row/column conventions. It determines all relations without relying on the inconsistent arrow labels.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The three-vertex quiver and its relations
notes: Three idempotent spaces \(L_1,L_2,L_3\), arrows \(e_{12},e_{21},e_{13},e_{31}\), product relations and a nilpotent central coordinate are drawn.
statement: For a left module over the matrix order, \(e_{ij}\) maps the \(j\)-th idempotent space to the \(i\)-th. The arrows between the central vertex and the other two obey the matrix-unit multiplication relations, with the relevant two-step products equal to the central parameter and mixed products determined by the remaining generators. For the single-character block, that parameter acts nilpotently.
fate: \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} verify the order and hence its module presentation. The right-hand notebook diagram reverses the \(e_{13}\) and \(e_{31}\) directions relative to this convention, while retaining the other pair; it cannot be repaired by one global transpose.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The rank-two order for SL3(R)
notes: The algebra \(M_4\oplus M_3\oplus M_3\oplus\mathbb C\) is restricted on the three walls \(z_1=0\), \(z_2=0\), \(z_1+z_2=0\) by vanishing and identification of matrix entries.
statement: Near the regular character of the trivial representation of \(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)\), the local category is represented by a nice order in \((M_4\oplus M_3\oplus M_3\oplus\mathbb C)\otimes\mathcal O(D)\). On \(z_1=0\), \(a_{13}=a_{14}=a_{23}=a_{24}=b_{12}=b_{13}=0\) and the lower right \(2\times2\) blocks of \(a,b\) agree; on \(z_2=0\), \(a_{12}=a_{14}=a_{32}=a_{34}=c_{12}=c_{13}=0\), with \(a_{22}=c_{22},a_{24}=c_{23},a_{42}=c_{32},a_{44}=c_{33}\); on \(z_1+z_2=0\), \(b_{13}=b_{23}=c_{13}=c_{23}=0\), \(b_{33}=c_{33}\).
fate: \citet[\S6, case \(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)\)]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} publish these explicit wall conditions. This is an exact match for the formulas, apart from the independent notebook diagram convention.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Compact weights in the PSL2(R) example
notes: For \(K\simeq\operatorname{SO}(2)\), the operator \(X_0=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) is said to have eigenvalues in \(2\mathbb Z\); admissibility, finite generation and bounded multiplicity are discussed.
statement: For the displayed real infinitesimal generator, a complex algebraic \(K\)-module has eigenvalues in \(2i\mathbb Z\) when the central element \(-I\) acts trivially. Integer weights are eigenvalues of \(X_0/i\). Harish--Chandra modules have finite multiplicities and, in this rank-one setting, bounded multiplicities; the conventions must be fixed before writing the truncating polynomial.
fate: \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} use integral labels for the \(K\)-types without confusing the normalized weight operator with the real compact generator.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The Casimir and bounded central support
notes: The notes again write \(4E_-E_+-H^2+2H\) as central and use its eigenvalues to localize the category.
statement: For the displayed standard \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) generators the central element is \(C=4E_-E_++H^2+2H\). Fixing a bounded region of its generalized spectrum is a rank-one instance of restricting central support.
fate: The Casimir and rank-one principal-series facts here are classical background, not first results of the 1978 local-category papers. The central-support theorem is \citet[\S3, Theorem~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1}. The sign error is visible on the complete scan of P000726 and is a faithful notebook error.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Morita functors in arbitrary matrix size
notes: The equivalence with \(M_\ell(\mathbb C)\)-modules is written using tensor product and \(\operatorname{Hom}\).
statement: For finite-dimensional left \(M_\ell(\mathbb C)\)-modules, evaluation gives a natural isomorphism \(\mathbb C^\ell\otimes\operatorname{Hom}_{M_\ell}(\mathbb C^\ell,V)\cong V\); these functors are inverse equivalences.
fate: This is elementary Morita equivalence, used as the model for the functor in \citet[\S4]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: A left ideal selecting finitely many compact weights
notes: A left ideal \(J\) is generated by \(\prod_{n=-N}^{N}(X_0-2n)\).
statement: With the normalized generator \(T=X_0/i\), let \(p_N(T)=\prod_{n=-N}^{N}(T-2n)\) and \(J=U(\mathfrak g)p_N(T)\). Then \(\operatorname{Hom}_{U(\mathfrak g)}(U(\mathfrak g)/J,V)\) identifies with \(\ker p_N(T)\), the sum of the selected \(K\)-weight spaces.
fate: The module/ideal identity in this item is elementary algebraic background; the subsequent block-equivalence theorem is a separate new assertion. This is the rank-one version of the finite-\(K\)-type construction in \citet[\S4]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1}. The factor \(i\) is required if one retains the notebook\textquotesingle s real generator.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The normalizer quotient algebra
notes: The normalizer is called the \ru{наименьшая} subalgebra containing \(J\) in which \(J\) is two-sided, and \(Q=N/J\).
statement: For a left ideal \(J\subset U\), the right normalizer \(N_U(J)=\{u\in U:Ju\subset J\}\) is the largest subalgebra of \(U\) containing \(J\) in which \(J\) is a two-sided ideal. The quotient \(N_U(J)/J\) is an algebra acting on vectors annihilated by \(J\), with the chosen left/right convention.
fate: The module/ideal identity in this item is elementary algebraic background; the subsequent block-equivalence theorem is a separate new assertion. \citet[\S4]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} use this normalizer construction. The scan explicitly says smallest; this is a faithful mathematical error, not a translation issue.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The finite-K-type functor
notes: The functor \(\tau\) retains the weight spaces with indices \(-N,\ldots,N\); \(Q\) acts on their sum.
statement: For an admissible \((\mathfrak g,K)\)-module \(V\), the selected sum \(\tau_N(V)=\bigoplus_{|n|\leq N}V_{2n}\) is finite-dimensional. The normalizer quotient acts because \(Jv=0\) implies \(Juv=0\) for \(u\in N_U(J)\).
fate: \citet[\S4]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} define the corresponding functor for a finite set of \(K\)-types.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: A sufficiently large finite set of K-types detects the block
notes: For bounded \(D\), taking sufficiently many compact weights is asserted to give the desired equivalence.
statement: For a bounded central-support region \(D\), a sufficiently large finite set of \(K\)-types can be chosen such that the associated normalizer-quotient functor is an equivalence on \(\mathcal C_D\); the algebra is finite over the center.
fate: \citet[\S4, Proposition~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} prove this and thereby establish their main theorem. A finite set independent of an arbitrary unbounded support region is not asserted.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Homogeneous-function principal series
notes: Functions on \(\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}\) homogeneous of degree \(s\) realize \(T^s\); on the circle, even trigonometric polynomials give the \(K\)-finite part.
statement: For \(f(tv)=|t|^s f(v)\), the even principal-series representation restricts to even Fourier modes on the circle. Differentiation gives \(E_+=x\partial_y\), \(E_-=y\partial_x\), \(H=x\partial_x-y\partial_y\), up to the overall action convention explicitly chosen.
fate: The principal-series family underlies \citet[\S5, Proposition~2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} and the rank-one calculation of \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Polynomial dependence on the principal-series parameter
notes: The matrix elements of the Lie algebra action in selected compact types are polynomial in \(s\), producing an algebra of matrix polynomials.
statement: After a fixed compact-picture realization and choice of finitely many \(K\)-types, the action of the normalizer quotient in principal-series families depends polynomially on the inducing parameter. The resulting representation embeds the quotient into a finite-dimensional endomorphism algebra tensored with the coordinate ring of the parameter space.
fate: \citet[\S5, lemma and Theorem~2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} prove precisely this polynomial realization.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Subquotients of principal series
notes: The notes suggest that every Harish--Chandra module appears as a subquotient of a principal-series representation.
statement: Every irreducible Harish--Chandra module is a subquotient of a suitable principal-series representation. This assertion does not say that every finite-length module, including nonsplit extensions with nonsemisimple central action, is a subquotient of one ordinary principal series with a fixed scalar infinitesimal character.
fate: \citet[\S5, Proposition~2(c)]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} state the irreducible result. The stronger literal formulation in the notes is unsupported and fails for modules with nonsemisimple central action.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Casimir eigenvalues in the homogeneous realization
notes: The eigenvalue is written \(-s^2+2s\), and reducibility is discussed at \(s=0,2\).
statement: For the displayed differential generators and homogeneity \((x\partial_x+y\partial_y)f=sf\), the correctly signed Casimir acts as \(s(s+2)\). Replacing the parameter by its negative gives \(s(s-2)\). The notebook\textquotesingle s scalar and reducibility parameter cannot both be used with its stated homogeneity convention.
fate: The Casimir and rank-one principal-series facts here are classical background, not first results of the 1978 local-category papers. The published treatment \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} instead uses a normalized parameter with central coordinate \(z=s^2-1\). The present identity is a direct editorial computation, not an attribution of the notebook formula to that paper.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The reducible principal series at the trivial character
notes: At \(s=0\), the constant function gives the trivial constituent and two remaining pieces are indicated; a second, dual reducibility point is shown at \(s=2\).
statement: At homogeneity degree zero, the even principal series contains the constants and has the two lowest/highest-weight discrete-series constituents as quotient. The contragredient extension occurs at degree \(-2\), not \(+2\), for this same homogeneity convention. The sequence is generally nonsplit.
fate: The Casimir and rank-one principal-series facts here are classical background, not first results of the 1978 local-category papers. \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} describe the three constituents and compute the local order from their selected \(K\)-types. Their normalized parameter differs from the notebook\textquotesingle s degree.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Generic Weyl reflection of the principal-series parameter
notes: The notes relate \(T^s\) and \(T^{2-s}\) away from exceptional parameters.
statement: For the homogeneous degree convention above, the generic intertwining equivalence is between degrees \(s\) and \(-s-2\). With the opposite parameter convention it is \(s\leftrightarrow2-s\); reducibility points require separate treatment, and a generic isomorphism need not extend as an invertible holomorphic family there.
fate: \citet[\S5, Proposition~2(b)]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local1} give the generic Weyl-orbit equivalence; \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} exploit it in the explicit order.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Three compact types near the trivial character
notes: The three weights \(-1,0,1\) are enough for the explicit algebra near the trivial character.
statement: With the normalized integral labels for the even \(K\)-types, retaining labels \(-1,0,1\) gives the local rank-three order for a sufficiently small neighborhood of the trivial infinitesimal character.
fate: \citet[\S5]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} explicitly choose these three types and compute the order.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Further groups proposed for explicit computation
notes: After listing rank-one groups and \(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)\), the notes suggest \(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb C)\), \(\operatorname{SU}(2,1)\), \(\operatorname{SO}(4,1)\), \(\operatorname{Sp}_4(\mathbb C)\), and the harder \(\operatorname{SL}_4\).
statement: This is a program to compute explicit local Harish--Chandra orders for additional groups. The central character, real form in the last example, neighborhood and equivalence convention are not all specified, so it is not one definite classification problem.
fate: \citet[\S6]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978local2} publish the listed low-rank examples, but do not identify or solve a single additional problem with all the notebook\textquotesingle s proposed groups and unspecified blocks.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the program is identifiable; the notes do not determine an exact additional problem whose full fate can be asserted.

title: An algebraic relation between commuting ordinary differential operators
notes: Krichever reports that the problem \([L_1,L_2]=0\) was treated by Burchnall and Chaundy in papers listed as 1922, 1928 and 1931.
statement: If scalar ordinary differential operators \(L_1,L_2\) with locally analytic coefficients commute, their orders are positive and their leading coefficients are normalized to one, then there is a nonzero polynomial \(Q\in\mathbb C[\lambda,\mu]\) such that \(Q(L_1,L_2)=0\). Coprimality of the orders is not required for this algebraic-dependence statement.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.1 and its proof]{krichever1978commutative} explicitly attribute and prove the Burchnall--Chaundy theorem. This confirms an old result, not a new theorem of the 1977 seminar. The earlier occurrence 1975-374.2 concerns the same spectral-curve line.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The rank-one spectral-curve description
notes: The older work is said to have posed and solved the classification for scalar operators of relatively prime orders, using algebraic geometry.
statement: A commuting rank-one ring of scalar ordinary differential operators is encoded by an algebraic spectral curve, a smooth marked point at infinity, a local parameter and rank-one sheaf data with a local trivialization. On a smooth curve in generic position this becomes a nonspecial divisor or line bundle; singular curves require torsion-free sheaves and cannot be omitted from an unrestricted classification.
reconstruction: The marked-point and sheaf data spell out what a modern classification needs; they are not all enumerated in this short announcement.
fate: \citet[introduction and \S1]{krichever1978commutative} confirm the local classification by Burchnall--Chaundy and distinguish it from the later effective reconstruction. This follows earlier seminar items 1975-374.5 and 1975-380.2; the latter\textquotesingle s smooth-curve-only scope remains a real qualification. The rank-one pointed-curve data also recur in 1975-383.9--383.12 and 1975-385.4--385.8, associated with GP-1975-14. The present historical classification remark does not itself restate the earlier inverse-construction question; GP-1975-26 concerns higher rank and is not an exact recurrence here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Theta formulas and linear motion on a Jacobian
notes: The historical construction is described as insufficiently effective: no theta functions, no straight-line Jacobian motion, and no recognition of conditional periodicity.
statement: For nonsingular rank-one spectral data, the Baker--Akhiezer construction yields explicit theta-function formulas and linearizes the commuting flows on the Jacobian. Quasiperiodicity and smooth real solutions require additional reality and nonsingularity assumptions; they do not hold for arbitrary complex or singular data.
fate: The underlying construction predates this talk: \citet[Theorem~1 and concluding discussion]{krichever1976zakharov}, received 8 October 1975 and published in 1976, construct the quasiperiodic solutions and announce theta formulas. \citet[\S1, pp.189--191]{krichever1977methods}, received 24 March 1977, give the explicit theta representation and Jacobian parameters. The 1978 restatement \citet[introduction and \S1]{krichever1978commutative} is the closest historical discussion, not the first appearance of the mathematical method.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Unspecified historical reference and almost-commuting pairs
notes: A 1939 paper is said to omit the older references, followed by the fragment that almost-commuting operators and Lax pairs exist.
statement: The author, title and equation of the 1939 paper are absent. The phrase almost commuting specifies neither a commutator nor a deformation parameter, so no definite mathematical proposition can be reconstructed from it.
fate: Comparison with \citet[introduction and bibliography]{krichever1978commutative} identifies the Burchnall--Chaundy line but does not resolve these two notebook fragments. No exact later result is assigned to them.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, these fragments remain unidentified; this is a source-identification limit, not evidence of an undeveloped mathematical problem.

title: Connections, curvature and local pure gauges
notes: The connection form \(A=A_\mu dx^\mu\), curvature \(dA+[A,A]\), gauge transformation and the flat-connection form are introduced; chiral fields are mentioned.
statement: For a compact matrix group, \(F_A=dA+A\wedge A\), or \(dA+\frac12[A\wedge A]\) when the bracket notation includes both antisymmetrized terms. A smooth flat connection is locally gauge-equivalent to the trivial connection, and globally so on a simply connected domain. A group-valued field produces a flat Maurer--Cartan form; a chiral field equation imposes additional conditions.
fate: This is background to the gauge-theoretic constructions of \citet[\S1]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} and the definitions in \citet[\S2.1]{dayapremawaldron2026parabolic}. The earlier occurrence 1975-386.1 treats Yang--Mills connections and action.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Topological charge requires a trace and normalization
notes: The integral of \(\varepsilon_{abcd}F^{ab}F^{cd}\) is said to be an integer up to a factor, without a written trace.
statement: For an \(\operatorname{SU}(2)\)-connection extending over \(S^4\), use anti-Hermitian matrices in the defining representation and define \(k=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)\in\mathbb Z\), with the sign of the integer fixed by orientation. A matrix-valued integral without the invariant trace is not a characteristic number.
fate: \citet[\S2.4]{dayapremawaldron2026parabolic} state a precise characteristic-number convention. The notebook\textquotesingle s coefficient cannot be compared without fixing the trace and component normalization.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Yang–Mills variation and the abelian case
notes: The action is the integral of \(\operatorname{Sp}(F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu})\), and the equation is \(\delta S=0\). Electrodynamics is assigned \(SU(1)\) or \(\mathbb R\).
statement: With a positive invariant inner product on the Lie algebra, the action is a positive multiple of \(\int|F_A|^2\), and its Euler--Lagrange equation is \(d_A^*F_A=0\). The compact abelian gauge group is \(U(1)\), whose Lie algebra is one-dimensional; \(SU(1)\) is trivial.
fate: \citet[\S1]{dayapremawaldron2026parabolic} state the action and equation. The \(SU(1)\) reading is visible on P000730 and is a faithful notebook error.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Classifying all finite-action Yang–Mills critical points
notes: The classical problem is to find all \(A\) satisfying the Yang--Mills equations and \(S(A)<\infty\).
statement: Classify, modulo smooth gauge transformations and with a fixed compact gauge group, smooth Yang--Mills connections on \(\mathbb R^4\) of finite \(L^2\)-curvature. After removable-singularity compactification this is the classification of Yang--Mills critical connections on bundles over the round \(S^4\), not merely their self-dual minima.
fate: The instanton part is explicitly classified by \citet[Theorem in \S4]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}. Nonminimal critical points exist, and \citet[\S1, Theorem~1.1]{dayapremawaldron2026parabolic} distinguish them from instantons and prove a low-energy deformation theorem. These results do not classify all finite-action critical points.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the instanton classification and substantial energy-gap results are established; the sources checked do not provide a full classification of all nonminimal Yang--Mills critical connections.
worth: A bounded energy or symmetry-restricted version is worth studying, because the full critical-point classification extends far beyond the instanton construction.

title: Finite action and extension over the point at infinity
notes: Requiring a field on \(S^4\) is called slightly stronger than finite energy on \(\mathbb R^4\).
statement: For a smooth Yang--Mills connection with compact structure group in dimension four, finite \(\int|F_A|^2\) implies smooth extension, after a gauge change, across the point at infinity on a suitable bundle over \(S^4\). For an arbitrary connection not satisfying Yang--Mills, the same conclusion is not supplied by this theorem.
fate: \citet[abstract and main removable-singularity result]{uhlenbeck1982removable} establish the equivalence for Yang--Mills fields. The result was announced in 1979 and fully published in 1982; the publisher page verifies both the result and the earlier announcement citation, although the full original proof was not accessible here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Four-dimensional conformal invariance
notes: The Euclidean metric and round sphere are conformally equivalent; the conformal group is written \(O(5,1)\), with a light-cone construction.
statement: In four dimensions the Hodge star on two-forms and the Yang--Mills action are conformally invariant. The conformal group of the round sphere is \(O(5,1)/\{\pm I\}\), with appropriate components for orientation preservation; \(S^4\) is the projectivized null cone in \(\mathbb R^{5,1}\). Pullback by smooth conformal diffeomorphisms preserves the equations. An arbitrary continuous map need not do so.
fate: Conformal geometry is part of the construction in \citet{atiyahward1977instantons}; \citet[\S1]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} explicitly fix the standard conformal structure on \(S^4\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The topological energy bound and self-dual minima
notes: The notes state \(S\geq n\), with a strict minimum at a self-dual field.
statement: With action \(E=-\int\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge *F)\) and charge as above, \(E\geq8\pi^2|k|\); equality holds exactly for one of \(F=\pm *F\), with sign chosen according to \(k\). The minimum is not strict along a nontrivial instanton moduli space or along gauge orbits.
fate: \citet[\S1 and \S2.4]{dayapremawaldron2026parabolic} state the minimizing role of instantons in a fixed bundle. The notebook suppresses the absolute value and normalization and overstates strictness.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Multi-instanton ansätze and the all-charge problem
notes: The notes attribute a \(5n+4\)-parameter family to \textquotesingle t Hooft, state completeness for charge two, and contrast it with dimension \(8n-3\).
statement: Explicit multi-instanton ansätze yield finite-dimensional subfamilies at each positive charge. Their raw parameter counts must be reduced by redundancies and gauge conventions: \(5n+4\) is not simultaneously a count of independent unframed moduli at \(n=2\), where \(8n-3=13\). Complete classification requires the more general linear algebra construction.
fate: \citet[p.2662, paragraph preceding the theorem]{atiyahhitchinsinger1977deformations} explicitly attribute the \(5n+4\)-parameter family to Jackiw, Nohl and Rebbi, distinguishing it from the \(5n\)-parameter family of \textquotesingle t Hooft. Their theorem gives \(8n-3\) independent unframed moduli. \citet[\S4]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} subsequently give all instantons for the classical compact groups. The notebook conflates the ansatz attribution and raw versus independent parameter counts.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Dimension of the SU2 instanton moduli space
notes: The dimension is \(8n-3\); an index calculation and removal of three gauge parameters are described.
statement: For charge \(k\geq1\) and the round metric on \(S^4\), the moduli space of irreducible \(SU(2)\) anti-self-dual connections modulo the full gauge group is smooth of real dimension \(8k-3\). The framed moduli space has dimension \(8k\). At charge zero the trivial connection has a nontrivial stabilizer and the same formula does not apply.
fate: \citet[theorem and proof, pp.2662--2663]{atiyahhitchinsinger1977deformations} prove smoothness and dimension \(8k-3\), using the self-dual deformation complex and vanishing of its obstruction space. Contributed 20 April 1977 and published in July 1977, this was available before the talk. Both pages of the primary scanned article were read.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The elliptic deformation complex and obstruction vanishing
notes: The duality equation is linearized; the cokernel is said to vanish by Hodge-theoretic considerations.
statement: For an anti-self-dual connection the deformation complex is \(\Omega^0(\operatorname{ad}E)\xrightarrow{d_A}\Omega^1(\operatorname{ad}E)\xrightarrow{d_A^+}\Omega^2_+(\operatorname{ad}E)\). On the round \(S^4\), the Weitzenböck formula gives \(H_A^2=0\); irreducibility gives \(H_A^0=0\), so the index is the local moduli dimension. Such cokernel vanishing is not automatic on arbitrary four-manifolds.
fate: This is the deformation argument underlying \citet{atiyahhitchinsinger1977deformations}; \citet[proof in \S3.2]{dayapremawaldron2026parabolic} explicitly use the same vanishing from positive scalar curvature and zero self-dual Weyl tensor.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Charge-one uniqueness and conformal symmetry
notes: For \(n=1\), all solutions are said to be spherically symmetric up to gauge; the five-dimensional moduli space and conformal stabilizer are discussed.
statement: Every charge-one \(SU(2)\) instanton on the round four-sphere is gauge-equivalent to a conformal transform of the basic instanton. Its unframed moduli are center and scale, giving a five-dimensional space. This is symmetry after choosing the corresponding conformal center and scale, not invariance under all rotations about an arbitrarily fixed point.
fate: \citet[p.2663, paragraph beginning with the conformal-group action]{atiyahhitchinsinger1977deformations} identify the charge-one moduli space with hyperbolic five-space, the orbit of the basic instanton. The same charge-one case is included in \citet[\S4]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}. The notebook\textquotesingle s group-dimension argument alone would not prove uniqueness, but the earlier primary theorem supplies the result.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Connectedness of fixed-charge instanton moduli
notes: The notes ask whether the space of instanton solutions is connected, with charge two singled out as incompletely understood.
statement: For each fixed positive charge \(k\), is the moduli space of \(SU(2)\) instantons on \(S^4\), modulo gauge, path-connected?
fate: Taubes proved the \(SU(2)\) statement in 1984. \citet[Theorem~1.2 and \S3.3]{dayapremawaldron2026parabolic} give a new proof in 2026 and explicitly distinguish Taubes\textquotesingle s original rank restrictions from the general \(SU(r)\) extension. Thus the precise question is solved, not an open problem inherited from the notebook.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, path-connectedness holds for every fixed-charge SU(2) instanton moduli space; the 2026 paper also states and proves the SU(r) version.

statement:
A consistent Euclidean pair, also recorded on P000741, is \(L_1=\lambda(

fate: \citet[\S5 and references7--8]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} identify the Belavin--Zakharov construction used in the notes. The corrected explicit pair is checked by expanding the polynomial commutator, not read into the differently signed P000732 display.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Orthogonal complex structures and the twistor fibration
notes: All linear complex structures on \(\mathbb R^4\) are said to be parameterized by one complex parameter, and \(S^7\to\mathbb CP^3\to S^4\) is drawn.
statement: The orientation-compatible orthogonal complex structures on a Euclidean four-space form \(SO(4)/U(2)\cong S^2\cong\mathbb CP^1\). All linear complex structures form a larger space. The twistor projection \(\mathbb CP^3\to\mathbb HP^1\cong S^4\) has fiber \(\mathbb CP^1\); it factors the quaternionic Hopf map through the circle quotient \(S^7\to\mathbb CP^3\).
fate: The twistor construction is the setting of \citet{atiyahward1977instantons} and \citet[\S1]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}. The notebook omits orthogonality and prints an inconsistent \(\mathbb CP^2\) fiber near the bottom of P000733.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Instantons as holomorphic bundles on twistor space
notes: The connection lifts to \(\mathbb CP^3\), defining an almost complex structure which is integrable precisely under the duality equations.
statement: The pullback of a unitary anti-self-dual connection to twistor space defines an integrable \(\bar\partial\)-operator. For the inverse correspondence one requires a holomorphic bundle trivial on every real twistor line and a compatible real or quaternionic structure with positivity. An arbitrary holomorphic bundle on \(\mathbb CP^3\) does not determine a unitary instanton.
fate: \citet[abstract]{atiyahward1977instantons} state the instanton/holomorphic-bundle identification; \citet[\S5]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} explicitly use this theorem in proving completeness. The full list of reality and line-triviality hypotheses is a modern reconstruction of the terse notes.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Integrability is involutivity of the complex tangent distribution
notes: An almost complex structure is described by local vector fields, which are required to commute.
statement: For a smooth almost complex structure \(J\), integrability is equivalent to involutivity \([T^{0,1},T^{0,1}]\subset T^{0,1}\), or vanishing Nijenhuis tensor. In holomorphic coordinates there is a commuting local frame, but an arbitrary frame of an integrable distribution need not commute. The base \(S^4\) is not thereby given a global complex structure.
fate: The notebook is invoking the classical complex integrability criterion in its twistor application; \citet[\S5]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} rely on the resulting holomorphic-bundle correspondence. This reference is thematic for the general criterion, not a claimed original proof of it.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Bounded analytic and inner functions
notes: \(H^\infty\) is the algebra of bounded analytic functions on the disk; inner functions have boundary modulus one almost everywhere.
statement: \(H^\infty(\mathbb D)\) consists of bounded holomorphic functions on the unit disk. An inner function has radial boundary values of modulus one for Lebesgue-almost every boundary point. The notation means \(|u(e^{it})|=1\), not multiplication of \(u\) by \(e^{it}\).
fate: \citet[\S1, opening definitions]{sznagy1976diagonalization} use precisely this setting, before the November 1977 talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Canonical factorization and the singular inner factor
notes: A bounded analytic function is decomposed as an inner factor times an outer factor, and the inner factor as a Blaschke product times an exponential built from a singular measure.
statement: Every nonzero \(u\in H^\infty\) has an inner--outer factorization. Its inner part is, up to a unimodular constant, a Blaschke product times \(S_\mu(z)=\exp\{-\int_{0}^{2\pi}(e^{it}+z)(e^{it}-z)^{-1}\,d\mu(t)\}\), for a finite positive singular measure \(\mu\). A positive exponent with positive measure gives the reciprocal and is generally unbounded.
fate: \citet[\S1 and the proof of Lemma~2]{sznagy1976diagonalization} invoke canonical factorization. The minus sign omitted in the notebook is mathematically necessary for the stated class.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Greatest common inner divisor
notes: The wedge \(\bigwedge_\alpha u_\alpha\) is described by a product over zeros and the lower bound of the singular measures.
statement: The greatest common inner divisor of a family of nonzero bounded analytic functions is determined, up to a unimodular factor, by the minimum zero multiplicities at each point and the greatest common lower bound of the singular measures of their inner factors. Zeros belonging to only one member do not contribute. For an all-zero family a separate convention is needed.
fate: \citet[\S1]{sznagy1976diagonalization} explicitly define the divisor for \(H^\infty\) families and use the all-zero value zero.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Failure of an unrestricted Bézout identity in H-infinity
notes: The notes deny that the greatest common inner divisor always has the form \(xu+yv\) with \(x,y\in H^\infty\).
statement: Having no common nonconstant inner divisor does not imply that \(xu+yv=1\) has bounded analytic solutions. Such an identity forces \(\inf_{z\in\mathbb D}(|u(z)|+|v(z)|)>0\), a condition stronger than inner coprimality. Thus \(H^\infty\) is not a Bézout domain in this sense.
fate: \citet[introduction and \S3]{sznagy1976diagonalization} explain why ordinary matrix equivalence must be replaced by quasi-equivalence. This supports the algebraic obstruction; the notebook gives no explicit counterexample.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The stronger outer-factor denial is not a complete statement
notes: A second denied identity has an outer factor \(h\) on one side and a heavily crossed-out mark on the other.
statement: The visible formula suggests a proposed Bézout identity after multiplication by an outer function, but its quantifiers, the crossed-out coefficient, and whether the factor is required to be invertible are not fixed. An exact strengthened negative assertion cannot be supplied responsibly.
fate: \citet[\S1, Lemma~2]{sznagy1976diagonalization} give the precise weaker generic-combination statement used next, but do not identify this damaged displayed denial.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, only the following Sherman lemma is securely identified; the stronger denial remains ambiguous.

title: Sherman’s generic linear-combination lemma
notes: For a fixed inner function \(\omega\), constants can be chosen so that \(u+tv=h_t(u\wedge v)\), with \(h_t\wedge\omega=1\); at most countably many \(t\) are exceptional.
statement: Let \(u,v\in H^\infty\) be not both zero, let \(d=u\wedge v\) and let \(\omega\) be inner. After writing \(u=da\), \(v=db\), the functions \(a,b\) have no common nonconstant inner divisor. For all but at most countably many complex \(t\), \(\omega\wedge(a+tb)=1\). Consequently \(u+tv=d h_t\) with \(h_t\wedge\omega=1\). Applying the lemma to the normalized pair is essential; the unnormalized identity \(\omega\wedge(u+tv)=\omega\wedge u\wedge v\) alone is a weaker statement.
fate: Exactly \citet[\S1, Lemma~2, pp.224--225]{sznagy1976diagonalization}, credited there to M. Sherman. The paper was received 1 November 1975 and published in 1976, so the talk is expository.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Finite polynomial combinations and simultaneous rows
notes: The notes extend the lemma to \(u_1+t u_2+\cdots+t^{r-1}u_{r+1}\), and then to finitely many rows.
statement: For a finite list \(u_1,\ldots,u_r\), divide by its common inner divisor. For any fixed inner \(\omega\), the polynomial combination \(u_1+t u_2+\cdots+t^{r-1}u_r\) is then inner-coprime to \(\omega\) outside a countable set of \(t\). One may avoid the union of the exceptional sets for finitely or countably many such rows. The last subscript in the notebook must be \(r\), not \(r+1\).
fate: \citet[\S1, Lemma~2 and \S2, Main Lemma]{sznagy1976diagonalization} establish the generic-combination mechanism and a stronger simultaneous \(\ell^1\)-coefficient theorem. The exact moment-curve wording in the notebook is a finite version; the paper\textquotesingle s Main Lemma does not insist on coefficients \(1,t,t^2,\ldots\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Matrix reduction by controlled inner divisors
notes: The final line mentions elementary transformations of a matrix.
statement: The generic-combination lemma can select combinations of rows or columns with prescribed common inner divisors and supports a quasi-equivalence diagonalization theory for finite and semi-finite \(H^\infty\)-matrices. It does not provide a Smith normal form under arbitrary invertible \(H^\infty\) row and column operations, nor settle all doubly infinite matrices.
fate: \citet[\S3]{sznagy1976diagonalization} carry out this program and explicitly separate the convergence difficulty for doubly infinite matrices. The notebook does not itself pose that larger question.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The KP normalization in the notes
notes: The equation is \(\frac34u_{yy}+\partial_x\{u_t+\frac14(6uu_x+u_{xxx})\}=0\).
statement: The recorded equation is \(3u_{yy}+(4u_t+6uu_x+u_{xxx})_x=0\), over complex variables when rational poles are considered. Rescalings or imaginary changes of \(y\) change the sign and strength of the corresponding particle interaction.
fate: The equation is already part of the earlier integrable-equation theory; see \citet[\S1, KP example]{krichever1977methods}. \citet[\S3]{krichever1978rational} print this normalization in the rational-pole context. The latter paper was received 6 September 1977 and appeared in the first issue of 1978; receipt is not by itself evidence of public circulation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The double-pole form of rational decaying KP solutions
notes: Every rational solution decreasing as \(x\to\infty\) is written as \(-2\sum_i(x-x_i(y,t))^{-2}\).
statement: On a parameter domain where poles are distinct, a rational KP solution tending to zero as \(x\to\infty\) has only double poles, zero simple-pole coefficients and leading coefficient \(-2\): \(u=-2\sum_{i=1}^N(x-q_i(y,t))^{-2}\). The pole coordinates can collide at exceptional parameters; a global assertion must allow the resulting limiting rational function.
fate: \citet[\S3, Theorem~3]{krichever1978rational} give the rational-solution characterization together with the associated Baker--Akhiezer function.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The particle Hamiltonian needs a normalization correction
notes: The \(y\)-motion is assigned to \(H=\frac12\sum p_i^2+\sum_{i<j}(x_i-x_j)^{-2}\).
statement: For precisely the displayed KP equation, the ansatz \(u=-2\sum(x-q_i)^{-2}\), and canonical momenta \(p_i=q_{i,y}\), Laurent coefficients give \(q_{i,yy}=-8\sum_{j\ne i}(q_i-q_j)^{-3}\). Thus one consistent canonical Hamiltonian is \(H=\frac12\sum p_i^2-4\sum_{i<j}(q_i-q_j)^{-2}\). Other standard Calogero conventions follow by rescaling or complexifying time and momenta; they must be stated.
reconstruction: The canonical convention \(p=q_y\) and the corrected coefficient are an editorial Laurent calculation. A different convention might explain the speaker\textquotesingle s numerical coefficient, but none is recorded.
fate: \citet[\S2, Theorem~2 and \S3, Corollary~1]{krichever1978rational} establish the pole/particle correspondence. Their Hamiltonian notation must be compared together with their time and Poisson conventions; no claim of an error in that published theorem is made here. The displayed notebook equation, ansatz and canonical convention \(p=q_y\) give the coefficients in the statement by direct Laurent expansion.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The KP time is a higher commuting particle flow
notes: The \(t\)-dependence is governed by a second commuting integral of the same particle system.
statement: In the same canonical convention, pole cancellation gives \(q_{i,t}=\frac34p_i^2-3\sum_{j\ne i}(q_i-q_j)^{-2}\). It is the position component of the flow generated by \(K=\frac14\sum_i p_i^3-3\sum_{i<j}(p_i+p_j)(q_i-q_j)^{-2}\), which commutes with the Hamiltonian of the preceding item. These compatible flows reconstruct the rational KP solutions where poles remain distinct.
reconstruction: The normalized Hamiltonian \(K\) is an editorial rewriting of the cubic flow; the notebook only names the additional commuting integral.
fate: \citet[\S3, Theorem~3 and Corollary~1]{krichever1978rational} identify the higher flow by a cubic trace invariant. The explicit coefficients here retain the notebook\textquotesingle s KP signs and canonical momenta rather than silently using a differently normalized \(F_3\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The differential-operator compatibility representation
notes: The notes write \(L_1=\partial_x^2+u\), \(L_2=\partial_x^3+\frac32u\partial_x+u\), and a zero-curvature relation.
statement: One consistent pair for the notebook\textquotesingle s KP normalization is \(L=\partial_x^2+u\), \(M=\partial_x^3+\frac32u\partial_x+w\), with \(w=\frac34u_x+\frac34\partial_x^{-1}u_y\), and \([\partial_y-L,\partial_t+M]=0\). The integration constant in \(\partial_x^{-1}u_y\) is fixed by boundary conditions or absorbed in a scalar gauge. The lower coefficient of the third-order operator is a new function \(w\), not simply \(u\).
reconstruction: The coefficient \(w\) and time sign are supplied by direct compatibility; the source has insufficient normalization information to infer them silently.
fate: The compatibility method and KP example already occur in \citet[Theorem~1]{krichever1976zakharov} and \citet[\S1]{krichever1977methods}. \citet[\S3]{krichever1978rational} use a separate scalar coefficient \(w\) in the rational-pole setting. The displayed pair is normalized directly to the notebook equation; the modern verification is not dated as a new 1978 theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Commutative subalgebras of Weyl skew fields
notes: A final proposal concerns commutative subalgebras of \(D_n\), the skew field associated with the Weyl algebra.
statement: The fragment suggests studying commutative subalgebras or subfields inside a Weyl skew field by spectral geometry. It specifies neither a class of subalgebras, a rank, a maximality condition, nor an equivalence relation; it is not a stated classification theorem for all \(n\).
fate: \citet{drinfeld1977commutative} is a contemporary primary lead, received 14 April 1976 and published in 1977, but its title and metadata alone do not verify a general Weyl-skew-field assertion. The notebook proposal remains too short to assign an exact fate.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, no definite new problem with specified quantifiers can be extracted from this fragment.

statement:
For a unitary connection \(

title: Gauge changes and removable frame singularities
notes: Changing a local frame gives \(A\mapsto u^{-1}du+u^{-1}Au\); apparent finite-point singularities are required to disappear in a suitable gauge. The covariant-derivative sum incorrectly repeats \(i\) as its summation index.
statement: In a local unitary frame, \(\nabla_\mu s_i=\sum_j A_\mu^{ij}s_j\), with a consistent row or column convention. Smoothness is a property of the connection on the bundle, not of one singular trivialization. Gauge equivalence preserves curvature up to conjugation and preserves self-duality.
fate: \citet[\S1]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} formulate regularity and equivalence in terms of bundles with connections. The displayed gauge law is standard; the index repair is elementary and scan-confirmed.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Regularity at infinity and compactification
notes: The connection and its bundle must extend over \(S^4=\mathbb R^4\cup\{\infty\}\); the extended bundle may be nontrivial.
statement: A regular instanton here means a smooth unitary self-dual connection on a bundle over the round four-sphere, expressed on the affine chart \(\mathbb R^4\). Extension over infinity is an imposed regularity condition in this talk. It should not be confused with a proof that arbitrary finite-action fields extend.
fate: This is precisely the sphere formulation in \citet[\S1]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}. The separate removable-singularity theorem is treated under record 432.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Clutching classification and charge
notes: Clutching along the equator gives \(\pi_3(U(r))=\mathbb Z\), generated by the block embedding of \(SU(2)\), and the sign of charge is reversed with duality.
statement: For \(r\geq2\), complex rank-\(r\) bundles over \(S^4\) are classified by an integer clutching class in \(\pi_3(U(r))\), equivalently the second Chern number after fixing orientation. For \(r=1\), \(\pi_3(U(1))=0\). This classifies underlying bundles, not their connections; a fixed charge supports a moduli space of instantons.
fate: \citet[\S1 and \S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} use the charge \(n\) and rank \(r\) as discrete parameters. The omitted rank-one exception and the distinction from gauge equivalence are essential.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Projection from a finite-dimensional trivial bundle
notes: The announced construction places \(L\) inside \(H\times S^4\), with \(\dim H=2n+r\), and obtains the connection by differentiating and orthogonally projecting.
statement: For the admissible instanton data described below, \(H\times S^4=L\oplus L^\perp\), with \(\operatorname{rank}L=r\), and \(\nabla s=P_L(ds)\). A Hermitian orthogonal projection gives a unitary connection. The sharp ambient dimension and the self-duality conditions belong to the instanton construction, not to an arbitrary connection embedding theorem.
fate: \citet[\S3 and \S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} give this construction; the announcement was received 27 November 1977, six days after the source date, and published in 1978.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Can every connection be induced from a trivial one?
notes: A bracketed question asks whether a bundle with connection can always be embedded into a trivial bundle with connection, comparing this with a Euclidean embedding of a Riemannian manifold.
statement: For a smooth Hermitian vector bundle over a finite-dimensional smooth manifold and a compatible unitary connection, does there exist a finite-dimensional trivial Hermitian bundle and an isometric bundle embedding for which orthogonal projection of the trivial connection is the prescribed connection?
reconstruction: The unitary compatibility and finite-dimensional smooth-base assumptions make the intended projection question precise.
fate: Affirmative before the talk: \citet[p.286, universal-connection theorem and the unitary case]{narasimhan1962universal} announce the joint Narasimhan--Ramanan theorem at the September 1961 Prague symposium; the proceedings appeared in 1962. The universal Stiefel connection gives exactly the projection formulation. Earlier occurrence 1975-382.5 describes the tautological universal connection and its base; it has no earlier problem identifier. That construction and this explicit universality question are closely related, with the quantifiers stated here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Quaternionic real structure and the twistor projection
notes: The map \(\sigma(z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4)=(-\bar z_2,\bar z_1,-\bar z_4,\bar z_3)\) has no invariant complex lines; its invariant complex two-planes are identified with \(S^4\). The following page calls \(\sigma\) an involution.
statement: On \(\mathbb C^4\), this antilinear map satisfies \(\sigma^2=-1\). It therefore induces a fixed-point-free involution on \(\mathbb{CP}^3\). Its invariant two-planes are quaternionic lines, parametrized by \(\mathbb{HP}^1\simeq S^4\). Sending \([z]\) to \(\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(z,\sigma z)\) is the twistor fibration with fiber \(\mathbb{CP}^1\).
fate: The twistor setting is already present in \citet{atiyahward1977instantons}; the precise real structure is written in \citet[\S0.2 and \S1.6]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons}. The latter is a detailed later exposition, not the first appearance of twistor space.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Affine coordinates of the twistor map
notes: Two complex quotients give \(x_2+ix_1\) and \(x_4+ix_3\), and a remark says that three coordinates suffice.
statement: On \((z_3,z_4)\ne(0,0)\), put \(x_2+ix_1=(z_1\bar z_3+\bar z_2z_4)/(|z_3|^2+|z_4|^2)\) and \(x_4+ix_3=(\bar z_2z_3-z_1\bar z_4)/(|z_3|^2+|z_4|^2)\). These are constant on the complex projective line associated with a quaternionic line. Three complex affine coordinates on \(\mathbb{CP}^3\) suffice; the statement is not a claim that three real coordinates parametrize \(S^4\).
fate: \citet[\S1.6]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons} print the coordinate construction in the detailed proof. It is an elementary coordinate expression of the earlier twistor map.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Self-duality as a type condition on pulled-back curvature
notes: The lemma says self-dual two-forms pull back to type \((1,1)\), while three complementary \((2,0)\) components are independent. Corollary (8) omits the component index on its bracket.
statement: For the indicated orientation, \(F=*F\) if and only if \((D^*F)^{2,0}=0\); for a unitary connection the conjugate \((0,2)\) condition follows. The three independent components detect the opposite-duality part. The condition \(D^*F=0\) without projection would force \(F=0\), since \(D\) is a surjective submersion.
fate: This is the local twistor criterion underlying \citet{atiyahward1977instantons} and made explicit in \citet[\S0.2 and \S1.6--1.9]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons}. The missing projection is a faithful notebook error.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.
