title: From a tensor subspace to the bundle fibers
notes: Choose \(I\subset H\otimes\mathbb C^4\), \(\dim I=n\). If \(\ell_1,\ell_2\) cut out a \(\sigma\)-invariant two-plane, take the orthogonal complement of \(I_{\ell_1}+I_{\ell_2}\).
statement: Write \(I_\ell=(1\otimes\ell)(I)\subset H\). For a quaternionic line \(D\subset\mathbb C^4\), let \(D^\circ\) be its annihilator and set \(L_D=(\sum_{\ell\in D^\circ}I_\ell)^\perp\). Choosing any basis \(\ell_1,\ell_2\) of \(D^\circ\) gives the same subspace, so the construction is independent of the two defining equations.
fate: \citet[\S2--\S3 and the unitary version in \S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} supply the linear-algebra construction. The independence is immediate from linearity of contraction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Rank, positivity, and quaternionic orthogonality conditions
notes: Conditions 1 and 2 prescribe fiber dimension \(r\) and positivity. Condition 0 is inserted later as \(Q(I_\ell,I_{\ell\circ\sigma})=0\).
statement: Require the contraction sum over every quaternionic line to have rank \(2n\), take a positive Hermitian form on \(H\), and impose the quaternionic orthogonality constraint. Since \(\ell\circ\sigma\) is antilinear, the second contraction must use the complex-linear form \(z\mapsto\overline{\ell(\sigma z)}\). With these admissibility conditions the orthogonal complements form a smooth rank-\(r\) bundle and the projected connection is self-dual.
reconstruction: Positivity on the ambient Hermitian space is adopted as the convenient modern sufficient hypothesis. The source\textquotesingle s claim that positivity follows from its abbreviated conditions is not independently strengthened here.
fate: The admissibility and projection theorem are in \citet[\S2--\S4 and \S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}. The detailed discussion of positivity appears in \citet[\S3--\S4]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons}. A bare indefinite form without the full conditions is insufficient.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Completeness and the equivalence relation on instanton data
notes: Theorem 1 says that the construction gives all self-dual Yang--Mills solutions and that nonisomorphic bundles correspond to inequivalent solutions. Isomorphisms of tensor diagrams are then described.
statement: Every regular unitary instanton on \(S^4\) is obtained from admissible finite-dimensional data. Two data sets yield gauge-equivalent connections precisely under the corresponding isomorphisms of diagrams, including an isometry on \(H\) and a change of basis in \(I\). The classification concerns bundles with connection; nonisomorphism of the underlying topological bundle is far too coarse.
fate: Exactly the completeness and uniqueness theorem of \citet[\S4]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual}, received 27 November 1977 and published in 1978; \citet[\S3]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons} provide the fuller proof. The upper tensor factor in the notebook diagram needs \(\mathbb C^4\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The quadruple-of-subspaces intervention
notes: Gelfand invokes unpublished work with Ponomarev on quadruples with an automorphism. Ponomarev takes the four images of \(H\) in \((H^{\oplus4})/I\), then asks for the quadruples compatible with an orthogonal-complement operation.
statement: The quotient construction indeed associates four subspaces to a tensor inclusion. But the notes do not specify the additional automorphism, nondegeneracy hypotheses, duality functor or equivalence relation needed for the claimed Hermitian classification; no exact classification theorem can be reconstructed.
fate: \citet{gelfandponomarev1971quadruples} is the earlier complex quadruple-classification lead, received 21 October 1970 and published in 1971. Its metadata do not verify the additional unpublished Hermitian assertion. The instanton diagram theorem of \citet[\S4]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} solves its own specified classification, not every possible quadruple-with-duality problem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the extra unpublished assertion remains unidentified; the earlier quadruple work is thematic evidence only.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand and V. A. Ponomarev

title: Gram matrices and the absence of horizontal sections
notes: A basis of \(I\) produces \(4n\) vectors \(e_{ij}\in H\) and their Gram matrix \(\widetilde Q\). The assumption \(\operatorname{rank}\widetilde Q=2n+r\) is equated with absence of horizontal sections.
statement: For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), write the basis tensor as \(e_i=\sum_{j=1}^4e_{ij}\otimes f_j\). The Gram matrix determines these vectors up to unitary equivalence on their span. Full rank \(2n+r\) means they span \(H\). For the instanton data, failure of spanning gives a constant orthogonal summand and hence a flat factor; the converse uses the admissibility theorem.
fate: \citet[\S6--\S7]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} state the full-span criterion and the horizontal-section interpretation. The notebook\textquotesingle s basis endpoint \(e_r\) must be \(e_n\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The constrained four-by-four Gram blocks
notes: Every block has the displayed six-parameter pattern; Hermitian symmetry and rank are required, while Conditions 1 and 2 are expressly omitted.
statement: The block pattern is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&0&c&d\\0&a&e&f\\f&-d&b&0\\-e&c&0&b\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). It expresses the quaternionic orthogonality equations. Global Hermitian symmetry relates the block at \((k,\ell)\) to the adjoint of the block at \((\ell,k)\). Positivity and the pointwise rank conditions remain necessary; the linear block pattern alone does not classify regular instantons.
fate: \citet[\S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} give the Gram-matrix formulation and explicitly acknowledge further regularity inequalities. Thus the notebook is an announcement of constraints, not an assertion that its listed linear equations suffice.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Affine generators of the orthogonal complement
notes: The vectors \(h_{k1}\) and \(h_{k2}\) are called \(2n\) global generators of \(L^\perp\) over \(S^4\), although their formulas use affine coordinates.
statement: On the chart \(\mathbb R^4\), the vectors \(h_{k1}=(x_2+ix_1)e_{k1}+(x_4-ix_3)e_{k2}+e_{k3}\) and \(h_{k2}=-(x_4+ix_3)e_{k1}+(x_2-ix_1)e_{k2}+e_{k4}\) span \(L_x^\perp\). They are not a global frame on \(S^4\) for nonzero charge: a rank-\(2n\) bundle globally generated by exactly \(2n\) independent sections would be trivial, contradicting \(c(L)c(L^\perp)=1\).
fate: \citet[\S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} use these vectors in affine Euclidean coordinates. The local construction extends geometrically across infinity after changing trivialization, not by retaining one global affine frame.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Computing the connection from a kernel and orthonormal frame
notes: Solve \(2n\) homogeneous equations in \(2n+r\) variables, choose a fundamental system, orthonormalize, and differentiate to obtain \(A_\mu^{ij}=Q(\partial_\mu y^{(i)},y^{(j)})\).
statement: On a chart where a chosen minor is nonzero, solve \(Q(v,h_{ka}(x))=0\), \(k=1,\ldots,n\), \(a=1,2\), for a local basis of \(L_x\). Its coefficients are rational functions of the real coordinates. Gram--Schmidt introduces square roots of positive rational functions. If \(Y\) is the resulting orthonormal column frame, the connection matrix is \(Y^*dY\), up to the notebook\textquotesingle s transposed frame convention.
fate: \citet[\S6]{drinfeldmanin1978selfdual} describe this explicit algorithm. Its formula is local and uses nonvanishing minors; no global rational orthonormal frame is implied.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The cohomological monad classification
notes: The final geometric theorem says diagrams classify bundles on \(\mathbb{CP}^3\) satisfying \(H^i(L(-2))=0\), the same for \(L^*\), and \(H^2(L(-1))=H^0(L(-1))=0\); the range of \(i\) is not stated.
statement: A precise published version defines an admissible locally free sheaf \(E\) by \(H^i(E(k))=0\) for \(i=0,1\) with \(i+k\leq-1\), and for \(i=2,3\) with \(i+k\geq0\). The middle cohomology of a special monad \(0\to I\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to H\otimes\mathcal O\to I^{\prime}\otimes\mathcal O(1)\to0\), with fiberwise injective and surjective end maps, gives an equivalence with admissible sheaves. Instantons additionally require the real and positivity conditions.
reconstruction: The full admissibility definition and monad exactness conditions are taken from the later theorem and are explicitly separated from the notebook\textquotesingle s abbreviated cohomology conditions.
fate: \citet[\S0.3--0.4 and Theorem~2.1]{drinfeldmanin1979instantons} prove this equivalence; the paper was received 26 May 1978 and published in 1979. The short notebook vanishings are a precursor, not an independently complete list with all quantifiers.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Hamiltonian formulation of a nonlinear scalar field
notes: The nonlinear Klein--Gordon equation is written with its Lagrangian, momentum \(\pi=u_t\), canonical bracket and energy.
statement: For a smooth real potential \(U(u)=m^2u^2/2+\varepsilon V(u)\), the formal Hamiltonian is \(H=\int[\pi^2/2+|\nabla u|^2/2+U(u)]\,dx\). The convention \(\{u(x),\pi(y)\}=\delta(x-y)\), \(u_t=\{u,H\}\), gives \(u_{tt}-\Delta u+U^{\prime}(u)=0\). Domain, boundary and regularity assumptions are needed for an actual infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian flow.
fate: \citet[introduction and \S1]{takhtajanfaddeev1974nonlinear} give the sine-Gordon instance before the talk. The general variational identity is standard background.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Free-field Fock energy and occupation densities
notes: The free Hamiltonian is diagonalized by Fourier modes; the occupation density in (7) contains \(a^*(k^{\prime})a(k)\) and the energy is a sum of relativistic one-particle energies.
statement: After normal ordering, the free bosonic Hamiltonian is \(d\Gamma(\omega)\), \(\omega(k)=\sqrt{|k|^2+m^2}\). On generalized momentum states its energy is \(\sum_j\omega(k_j)\). The formal occupation density is \(a^*(k)a(k)\), or rigorously its smeared number operator; sharp-momentum states and delta-function occupations are distributions, not normalizable eigenvectors.
fate: \citet[\S1, pp.148--149 of the Russian text]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} use exactly this particle interpretation. The prime on the first argument in the notebook is a scan-confirmed error.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Nonspreading finite-energy solutions and failure of free scattering
notes: Solitons are first called everything failing to approach a free solution, then more narrowly finite-energy solutions that do not spread out.
statement: A localized stationary or traveling solution can obstruct scattering to a free Klein--Gordon wave. Non-scattering alone is not a definition of a soliton: it also includes other recurrent dynamics and, outside a global-existence class, breakdown of the solution. The intended soliton notion here is a localized coherent structure whose energy remains concentrated in a moving bounded region.
fate: \citet[introduction, pp.4--6]{faddeevkorepin1978quantum} make the same distinction between spreading waves and localized structures; \citet[\S4]{takhtajanfaddeev1974nonlinear} supply explicit sine-Gordon kinks and breathers.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Lorentz boosts and the mass-shell relation
notes: Boosting a static finite-energy solution gives \(u_s((x-x_0-vt)/\sqrt{1-v^2})\) and \(H_s(v)=M/\sqrt{1-v^2}=\sqrt{p^2+M^2}\).
statement: For a localized static solution of a Lorentz-invariant scalar equation in one spatial dimension, a boost with \(|v|<1\) gives the displayed traveling profile. If \(M\) is its rest energy, the conserved energy-momentum vector gives \(E=M/\sqrt{1-v^2}\) and \(p=Mv/\sqrt{1-v^2}\). Boundary stress must vanish so the integrated charges transform correctly.
fate: \citet[\S1, equation~(2)]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} state this explicitly for the sine-Gordon kink. The notebook\textquotesingle s schematic higher-dimensional opening does not turn the one-coordinate boost formula into a general \(d\)-dimensional expression.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Resolution into radiation and finitely many localized structures
notes: Equation (12) proposes \(u\to u_0+\sum u_s\) at large positive and negative time, calling it a hypothesis in general and a theorem in models. The next page explicitly adds periodic localized solutions.
statement: A precise model question is whether every global finite-energy sine-Gordon solution admits a large-time decomposition into finitely many localized coherent structures, including kinks, antikinks and breathers, plus radiation, in a specified topology. The notebook supplies neither a convergence norm nor genericity assumptions; it first writes a free-wave term and then explicitly adds periodic localized structures.
reconstruction: The all-energy sine-Gordon formulation makes the model and quantifiers explicit. The inclusion of breathers is supported by P000748; the exact radiation topology remains to be specified rather than attributed to the notebook.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.1, Definition~2.6 and Theorem~10.1]{chenliulu2020sinegordon} prove resolution for generic data in \(H^{2,s}_{\sin}\times H^{1,s}\), \(s>1/2\); their radiation has modified scattering inside the light cone. The preprint first appeared 8 September 2020; the version read is 15 February 2022. This is a partial match to the unrestricted wording, not a theorem of free scattering for all energy data.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the cited generic weighted-data result is established. This search did not verify an all-finite-energy theorem matching the notebook wording. The verified theorem uses modified scattering for its radiation component.
worth: Worth developing in a carefully bounded form, because identifying the admissible coherent structures and the convergence topology prevents a false soliton-resolution assertion.

title: Additivity of asymptotic energies
notes: The notes pass from separated soliton asymptotics to \(H(u)=H(u_0)+\sum H_s(v_i)\).
statement: Energy additivity follows if the asymptotic decomposition converges strongly enough in the energy quantities and the interaction terms vanish as the localized profiles separate. Pointwise convergence alone is insufficient. In a long-range model the radiation energy may have a nonlinear scattering description even though its conserved energy is well-defined.
fate: \citet[introduction, equation~(1.13)]{faddeevkorepin1978quantum} explicitly assume separation of the wave packet and localized solutions; \citet[\S4, equations~(32)--(33)]{takhtajanfaddeev1974nonlinear} obtain an exact spectral energy decomposition in the integrable sine-Gordon setting.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Several particle species from one classical field
notes: Quantization is expected to give sums of ordinary-particle and soliton energies, although only one scalar field occurs in the Lagrangian; soliton contributions persist in the classical limit.
statement: The semiclassical particle interpretation assigns species to stable localized classical solutions and their quantized internal excitations. In sine-Gordon the kink mass scales as inverse coupling. The displayed additive spectrum describes asymptotic multiparticle states; it is not a proof that an arbitrary nonlinear field has a rigorously constructed Fock decomposition or that all species are independent.
fate: \citet[\S1 and conclusion]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} already formulate this semiclassical interpretation. In the exact sine-Gordon spectrum the lightest breather is identified with the perturbative neutral particle, so counting both as independent species would duplicate a state.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Periodic solitons and their internal parameters
notes: A periodic localized solution has center, velocity, period parameter \(\beta\) and initial phase \(\alpha\). Equation (18) then writes \(\sqrt{p_k^2+M(\alpha_k)}\).
statement: A breather has a frequency or action parameter controlling its rest energy and a separate phase parameter. Relativistic energy is \(\sqrt{p^2+M(\beta)^2}\) if \(\beta\) denotes that internal parameter. It is independent of the initial time phase. Thus (18) needs both the mass square and a parameter-name correction relative to the sentence immediately before it.
fate: \citet[\S1, equation~(3) and subsequent discussion]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} distinguish phase from the internal action and give the breather mass. Both defects in the notebook formula are visible in the scan.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Classical sine-Gordon kink and breather masses
notes: For \(u_{tt}-u_{xx}+m^2\sin u=0\), introducing coupling \(\gamma\) gives kink mass \(8m/\gamma\) and breather mass \((16m/\gamma)\sin\alpha\).
statement: Use \(H=\gamma^{-1}\int[\frac12u_t^2+\frac12u_x^2+m^2(1-\cos u)]dx\) and \(\{u(x),u_t(y)\}=\gamma\delta(x-y)\). The kink has energy \(8m/\gamma\). A breather with frequency \(m\cos\alpha\), \(0<\alpha<\pi/2\), has rest energy \((16m/\gamma)\sin\alpha\). The endpoint \(\alpha=\pi/2\) is a separatrix limit, not a finite-period breather.
fate: \citet[\S4]{takhtajanfaddeev1974nonlinear} give these masses and explicit solutions; \citet[\S1]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} retain them. The source reverses the bracket order in (21) without changing its sign, unlike (3); the canonical convention is fixed here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Bohr--Sommerfeld breather levels and the exact coupling
notes: The internal angle is quantized as \(\alpha=\gamma n/16\), attributed approximately to Takhtajan--Faddeev, 1974.
statement: This is a semiclassical level rule with an upper bound on \(n\). In the exact sine-Gordon scattering convention with Lagrangian coupling \(\beta^2\), write \(\Gamma=\beta^2/(1-\beta^2/(8\pi))\). Bound-state masses satisfy \(m_n=2M\sin(n\Gamma/16)\), \(1\leq n<8\pi/\Gamma\). The bare or classical coupling must not silently be identified with \(\Gamma\).
fate: \citet[\S1 and \S5]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} discuss the semiclassical rule in 1975. \citet[equation~(2)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp} state the exact mass-ratio formula in May 1977. The notebook\textquotesingle s approximate 1974 attribution is not used to date the full quantum result.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Rigorous construction of exponential interactions at small coupling
notes: Glimm, Jaffe and Fröhlich are invoked for rigorous small-coupling quantization, beside the expression \(m^2\gamma^{-1}(1-\cos\gamma u)\). Equation (26) writes \([\pi(x),u(y)]=i\delta(x-y)\), in the opposite order to the earlier Poisson bracket.
statement: Rigorous construction requires a specified normal ordering, ultraviolet limit, volume limit and normalization. The notebook\textquotesingle s potential has quadratic term \(m^2\gamma u^2/2\); it is not the canonically normalized potential \(m^2\beta^{-2}(1-\cos\beta\varphi)\) with small-oscillation mass \(m\). A theorem for a massive reference field is not automatically an identical theorem for every massless-reference sine-Gordon formulation.
reconstruction: With the convention used in item 1977-436.1, canonical quantization gives \([u(x),\pi(y)]=i\delta(x-y)\). The source changes the bracket order without specifying a corresponding sign convention.
fate: \citet[abstract]{froehlich1975quantized} announced a Wightman theory for a sine-Gordon interaction with a nonvanishing mass term in March 1975. The accessible primary abstract supports the historical construction claim, but does not verify every omitted hypothesis of the notebook\textquotesingle s Hamiltonian statement.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Short-range wave operators and a unitary scattering operator
notes: For \(H=-\Delta/(2m)+v\), with rapidly decaying \(v\), the double-time expression defines a unitary \(S\)-operator.
statement: For a real bounded short-range potential, for example \(|v(x)|\leq C\langle x\rangle^{-1-\epsilon}\), the wave operators \(W_\pm=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_0}\) exist and have range \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)\). Their completeness implies \(S=W_+^*W_-\) is unitary on the free Hilbert space. Bound states are not additional scattering channels; decay without self-adjointness assumptions is insufficient.
fate: The established short-range theorem is restated with proof in \citet[Theorem~2.4 and \S1]{yafaev2004lectures}, lectures delivered in 2001 and posted in 2004. This later exposition is used to check precise hypotheses, not to date the old scattering theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Extracting scattering amplitudes from propagator asymptotics
notes: Equations (30)--(31) evaluate the propagator along free classical rays and divide by free propagators to recover a momentum-space scattering kernel.
statement: The useful assertion is a distributional large-time extraction after testing against momentum wave packets and retaining the stationary-phase normalization. A pointwise quotient of kernels with omitted normalization is not, by itself, a well-defined equality for a scattering distribution. The required free rays are \(x=pt/m\).
reconstruction: Only the distributional, wave-packet interpretation is asserted here; the exact normalization cannot be recovered from the notebook\textquotesingle s formula alone.
fate: \citet[\S2.1, equations~(1.3)--(1.11)]{faddeevkorepin1978quantum} present the corresponding prescription with its normalization and illustrate it by spectral expansion. The primary article was received 4 July 1977 and published in June 1978; the notebook\textquotesingle s ratio is an abbreviated precursor.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The stationary-phase exponent and amplitude
notes: Equation (32) gives \(\widetilde\Psi(mx/t)e^{ix^2/(2mt)}\) for an integral with phase \(px-p^2t/(2m)\).
statement: For the convention \(\Psi(x,t)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int\widehat\Psi(p)e^{i(px-p^2t/(2m))}dp\), \(m>0\), and Schwartz amplitude, the leading term as \(t\to+\infty\) on bounded velocity ranges is \(\sqrt{m/(2\pi t)}e^{-i\pi/4}e^{imx^2/(2t)}\widehat\Psi(mx/t)\). Both the mass position in the exponent and the power of \(t\) matter.
fate: This follows directly from the critical point \(p=mx/t\) and Hessian \(-t/m\). Compare \citet[equation~(2.8)]{yafaev2004lectures} in the normalization \(H_0=-\Delta\). The notebook error is faithfully transcribed.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Path integrals with soliton boundary data
notes: Time-sliced mechanical and field path integrals are written, and sums of solitons are imposed as initial and final configurations to define transition quantities.
statement: These oscillatory path integrals encode propagators and, after asymptotic normalization, scattering amplitudes. They require regularization, renormalization and appropriate boundary conditions; an unqualified infinite product of Lebesgue measures does not define a continuum measure. A complex amplitude is not itself a transition probability.
fate: \citet[\S2--\S3]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} already use this stationary-phase and renormalization scheme in 1975; \citet[\S2.2]{faddeevkorepin1978quantum} develop the general soliton boundary prescription in the 1978 review.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: A quantum inverse-scattering method
notes: The notes say that there is not yet a good quantum version of the inverse problem.
statement: Construct quantum scattering-data operators and exchange relations that generate commuting quantum integrals and eigenstates for a specified integrable field model. This is a definite method problem when the model and operator algebra are fixed; it is not an existence theorem for every possible quantization.
fate: \citet[\S2--\S4]{sklyaninfaddeev1978quantum} give an early quantum inverse-scattering construction, received 28 July 1978 and published in December 1978. They explicitly construct the nonlinear-Schrödinger operators, while stating that the corresponding comparison with classical sine-Gordon variables had not yet been completed. Thus the early result has a precise model-dependent scope.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The exact sine-Gordon scattering matrix has two charge channels
notes: Zamolodchikov\textquotesingle s guessed exact formula is cited. Equation (46) then writes a single phase times momentum-conserving delta functions for a soliton and an antisoliton.
statement: The sine-Gordon two-particle matrix has transmission and reflection amplitudes in the soliton--antisoliton sector, with unitarity, crossing and prescribed bound-state poles. A single scalar phase describes an appropriate eigenchannel or reflectionless specialization; it is not the generic full charge-channel matrix.
fate: \citet{zamolodchikov1977exact} was received 4 January 1977 and published in June 1977. The separately opened primary announcement \citet[equations~(4)--(10)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp}, submitted 14 April and published 20 May 1977, explicitly displays both amplitudes. This was available before the talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Classical solvability versus quantum solvability
notes: The hypothesis says that every classically solvable problem is solvable in its quantum version.
statement: The source specifies neither solvability, quantization, preservation of integrals, domains, nor a class of models. Quantum anomalies and ordering choices are relevant to any precise formulation, so no universal yes-or-no proposition can be extracted without adding substantial hypotheses.
fate: \citet[\S2]{sklyaninfaddeev1978quantum} provide a successful model construction, not a theorem that all classically integrable systems admit the required quantization. No exact fate is assigned to the unrestricted sentence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the general sentence remains under-specified. The precise quantum inverse-scattering method is treated separately.

title: The fluctuation determinant and the sine-Gordon zero mode
notes: Expanding around \(U_{cl}\) produces a Hessian and determinant. For a stationary soliton the notes give \(q(x)=1/\cosh^2x\), call it a Bargmann potential, and refer to a zero eigenfunction.
statement: For the sine-Gordon kink, the spatial Hessian is \(K=-\partial_x^2+m^2(1-2\operatorname{sech}^2(mx))\). Its translation mode \(u_s^{\prime}\) has eigenvalue zero. A determinant must remove this mode and account for the collective coordinate; the relevant object is a renormalized determinant ratio. The isolated positive \(\operatorname{sech}^2x\) is not this Hessian potential.
fate: \citet[\S2, equations~(12)--(18)]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} explicitly exclude the zero mode, use the reflectionless spatial operator and express the determinant through spectral/scattering information. This is a precise earlier match after the source\textquotesingle s missing sign, coefficient and constant are restored.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Explicit higher-loop functionals of the resolvent kernel
notes: The next-loop discussion calls for \(R=A^{-1}\), its kernel, and \(\int R^3(x,x)\,d^2x\), with the hope that such quantities can be calculated explicitly.
statement: The expression is ambiguous between the diagonal of an operator cube and the cube of a coincident kernel; zero modes, boundary conditions, ultraviolet subtraction and counterterms are unspecified. It therefore does not define one finite invariant whose exact evaluation can be tracked.
fate: \citet[\S3 and \S4]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} discuss renormalized higher-loop diagrams and explicitly report their computational difficulty. This identifies the setting but not an exact value or theorem for the notebook\textquotesingle s ambiguous functional.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the displayed functional remains insufficiently specified; it is not entered as an allegedly untouched open problem.

title: The one-loop sine-Gordon mass correction
notes: The stated expansion is \(M=8m/\gamma-m/\pi+O(\gamma)\).
statement: In the weak-coupling sine-Gordon normalization and the mass-renormalization convention used in the semiclassical calculation, the one-loop kink mass is \(M=8m_r/\gamma-m_r/\pi+O(\gamma)\). A finite renormalization of the mass parameter changes higher coefficients, so the symbol \(m\) must be specified when comparing schemes.
fate: \citet[\S2, following equation~(18), and \S3]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} already give this result in 1975, with \(m_r\) the renormalized mass. The 1978 review is not its first publication.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The no-higher-corrections claim depends on the mass convention
notes: The notebook conjectures the exact identity \(M=8m/\gamma-m/\pi\), attributed to Zamolodchikov\textquotesingle s justification.
statement: Without defining the renormalized parameter \(m\), the all-orders statement is not determinate. For the physical lightest-breather mass \(m_1\) and the Lagrangian coupling \(g=\beta^2\), the exact ratio is \(M/m_1=[2\sin(\pi\xi/2)]^{-1}\), \(\xi=g/(8\pi-g)\). Its expansion is \(8/g-1/\pi+g/192+O(g^2)\), so the two-term expression is not exact in that physical-mass convention.
reconstruction: The Taylor expansion in the physical mass convention is an editorial algebraic consequence of the published ratio; it is not a claim that the notebook used that convention.
fate: The mass-ratio identity follows from \citet[equation~(2)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp}. \citet[\S2--\S3]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} explicitly frame the earlier conjecture as the possibility that higher corrections reduce to renormalization. The source does not fix the convention needed to decide its literal all-orders wording.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the exact mass ratios are known in the specified sine-Gordon convention. The notebook\textquotesingle s bare claim cannot be labeled convention-independently true or false.

title: The coupling threshold is not simply soliton disappearance
notes: The last sentence says everything is fine for \(\gamma\leq8\pi\), beyond which the soliton disappears.
statement: The threshold \(\beta^2=8\pi\) concerns the quantum sine-Gordon interaction and its renormalization. It does not follow from extrapolating a one-loop mass to zero. Breather bound states already cease to exist when \(\xi\geq1\), equivalently \(\beta^2\geq4\pi\), while soliton and antisoliton scattering persist in the repulsive regime below \(8\pi\). Endpoint claims require separate hypotheses.
fate: \citet[abstract]{coleman1975equivalence} discuss unbounded energy density beyond \(8\pi\) in the stated convention; \citet[equation~(2)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp} distinguish the bound-state threshold. Neither supports the notebook\textquotesingle s unrestricted disappearance sentence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Semiclassical phase integrals and reflectionless couplings
notes: The abbreviated action gives an integral for the scattering phase. The notes replace it by a sum at \(\gamma=8\pi/N\) and describe interpolation to arbitrary coupling.
statement: The semiclassical phase is obtained from the two-soliton action after subtracting asymptotic external contributions. A finite-product exact scattering formula occurs at reflectionless values \(\Gamma=8\pi/N\), where \(\Gamma\) is the renormalized coupling of the exact scattering formula. In terms of \(\beta^2\), these values are \(8\pi/(N+1)\). A logarithm branch and analytic continuation must be fixed in the phase integral.
fate: \citet[\S4, equations~(27)--(30)]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} derive the semiclassical phase; \citet[equations~(7)--(10)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp} explicitly discuss the reflectionless interpolation. The notebook uses one symbol for distinct coupling conventions.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The hyperbolic-secant scattering analogy
notes: Sine-Gordon scattering is said to resemble a one-dimensional Schrödinger system \(-d^2/dx^2+a/\cosh^2(\alpha x)\); a possible eigenvalue formula is crossed out.
statement: This is an analogy with the explicitly solvable hyperbolic-secant potential. At special negative strengths \(a=-\ell(\ell+1)\alpha^2\), \(\ell\) a nonnegative integer, the Schrödinger potential is reflectionless. The notebook gives no parameter map identifying its entire Schrödinger spectrum with the quantum field theory, and the deleted eigenvalue is not restored as a theorem.
fate: The exact reflectionless fluctuation operator in \citet[\S2, equation~(16)]{korepinfaddeev1975quantization} and reflectionless quantum scattering in \citet[equation~(7)]{zamolodchikov1977jetp} explain the comparison. They do not identify a literal equivalence of the two Hamiltonians.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: The constrained sphere sigma model and its classical Lax representation
notes: The closing example is \(n:\mathbb R^{1,1}\to S^n\), with Lagrangian \(\frac12\int\partial n\cdot\partial n\,dx\), and a Lax pair attributed to Pohlmeyer and to Zakharov--Mikhailov.
statement: For a unit vector field \(n\in S^n\), the constrained Euler--Lagrange equation is \(\Box n+(\partial_\mu n\cdot\partial^\mu n)n=0\). Its nonlinearity comes from the constraint. The classical sphere sigma models admit a spectral-parameter zero-curvature formulation and conserved quantities; this does not by itself construct their quantum theory.
fate: \citet{pohlmeyer1976integrable} appeared in 1976, received 28 August 1975. \citet[introduction, \S3 and \S6]{zakharovmikhailov1978relativistic}, submitted 4 January 1978 and published June 1978, explicitly identify Pohlmeyer\textquotesingle s sphere-model result and develop the reduction and integration scheme. Thus the classical claim was already known; the latter article is not treated as a theorem of integrability for all homogeneous spaces.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.

title: Massive sigma-model particles scatter like solitons
notes: The scan reads \ru{Массивные частицы рассеиваются как солитоны}; both transcriptions instead say that particles appear as solitons.
statement: The intended comparison is elastic, factorized scattering of massive quantum particles: multiparticle amplitudes are assembled from two-particle amplitudes, with no particle production in the integrable description. It is not a claim that all these particles are classical topological kink solutions.
reconstruction: The reading of the Russian verb was checked independently against the scan by both this record editor and the chapter assembler.
fate: \citet[\S1--\S3]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on} construct an \(O(N)\)-invariant factorized matrix for \(N\geq3\) and support its sigma-model identification by perturbative comparisons, expressly distinguishing that identification from the algebraic construction. The article was received 22 August 1977, revised 14 November 1977, and published in February 1978. This closely matches the scattering remark but is not a proof of a fully axiomatized field theory.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope.
